quiz.why: Lily is the baby girl Mitchell and Cameron adopt from Vietnam.

quiz.q: Why does Manny live with Jay?
options: His mother Gloria has married Jay
quiz.why: Gloria and Manny move into Jay's house after Jay and Gloria marry.

quotes.note: Mitchell introduces himself by his job, which tells us how serious he is.
Gloria says it proudly, and it explains part of the family's culture.

truefalse.s: Jay is Claire and Mitchell's father.
Gloria is from Colombia.
Mitchell and Cameron adopt a baby girl called Lily.
Phil is Jay's son.
truefalse.fix: Phil is married to Claire, Jay's daughter.

truefalse.s: Manny is Gloria's grandson.
truefalse.fix: Manny is Gloria's son.

truefalse.s: The three families live in the same house.
truefalse.fix: They live in different houses and meet for dinner.

shortAnswers.q: Why does Phil try so hard to be a 'cool dad'?
shortAnswers.model: He wants his children to like him more than they respect him. He is also a little insecure about being the fun parent.

shortAnswers.q: What does the episode suggest about how different families can still be close?
shortAnswers.model: It suggests that love and effort matter more than tradition. The three families are very different, but they keep showing up for each other.

shortAnswers.q: Would you want a camera crew following your family? Why?
shortAnswers.model: No, because we would start performing for the camera instead of being ourselves. Some family moments should stay private.

shortAnswers.q: Why does Jay find it difficult to accept Manny at first?
shortAnswers.model: He is not used to being a stepfather, and Manny is strange and very direct. Jay needs time to see that Manny is part of his new family.

gaps.line: The ocean is the largest ___ on Earth.
gaps.hint: the natural home of a plant or animal

gaps.line: We are the first generation to know we are ___ the planet.
We need to live in ___ with nature.
Nature is not a place to visit. It is our ___.
This is a story of ___.

quiz.q: Which place does the episode show with a great animal migration?
quiz.why: The episode follows the huge herds of the Serengeti and the animals that hunt them.

quiz.q: By how much does the episode say wildlife has fallen in fifty years?
quiz.why: It reports that wild animal populations have fallen by around sixty per cent.

quiz.q: Why does the episode end with a message of hope?
options: It says we can still fix the damage
It says the planet is already saved
It says animals do not need help
quiz.why: The final message is that the future is not decided yet and people can still act.

quotes.quote: This is the only home we have.
quotes.note: The narrator says it to remind viewers that there is no second planet.
It is the episode's final note of hope.

truefalse.s: The episode is narrated by David Attenborough.
The episode shows animals and places from different parts of the world.
The episode says that everything in nature is connected.
The episode says wildlife has grown in the last fifty years.
truefalse.fix: It says wildlife has declined sharply in the last fifty years.

truefalse.s: The episode is set only in Africa.
truefalse.fix: It travels to many continents and oceans.

truefalse.s: The episode says humans cannot change the planet.
truefalse.fix: It says humans have the power to change the planet, for good or bad.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the episode show the same message in different places?
shortAnswers.model: It wants to show that the same problems affect very different habitats. That makes the damage feel global rather than distant.

shortAnswers.q: What does the ending suggest about the future?
shortAnswers.model: It suggests that the future is still open, but only if people act soon. The film ends with hope, not with a promise.

shortAnswers.q: Would you change anything in your life after watching? Why?
shortAnswers.model: I would try to waste less and buy fewer things I do not need. The programme makes it clear that small habits add up.

shortAnswers.q: Why does Attenborough say the natural world is our greatest ally?
shortAnswers.model: Because healthy nature gives us clean air, water and food. Protecting it is also protecting ourselves.
